reason: B is honestly labelled throughout, has an operable artifact in the first screen at 1440 and passes axe with zero violations. A presents an invented city, agenda, volunteer sign-offs and coverage history as real, and routes its primary action to an email address the brief never supplied. B's flaws (late disclosure of the no-backend state, the long-input layout blowout, a thinner clerk/Spanish path) are fixable in an hour. I would change my mind only if A's mailto address and 'real' framing were cleared as brief-supplied, since A's code organisation and Spanish/clerk coverage are otherwise slightly stronger.
